question: Unconventional (non-traditional) machining removes material mainly by…
options: A sharp tool that is harder than the work
Melting the whole job and recasting it
Energy forms such as sparks, light, chemicals or jets
Pressing the work into a shaped die
explanation: Non-traditional processes use electrical, thermal, chemical, electrochemical or jet energy instead of a sharp tool in contact.

question: Which is a main reason for using unconventional machining?
options: Very hard materials and complex shapes with no cutting force
It is always cheaper than plain turning
It needs no electricity or energy at all
It works only on soft plastics and rubber
explanation: They suit very hard/brittle materials, complex shapes, tiny holes and delicate parts where tool forces must be avoided.

question: Unconventional machining processes are classified on the basis of…
options: The colour of the finished job
The type of energy used to remove material
The size and weight of the machine
explanation: Mechanical, thermal (electrothermal), electrochemical and chemical.

question: EDM and laser-beam machining belong to which energy class?
explanation: EDM, WEDM, LBM, EBM and PAM remove material by local melting and vaporisation.
ref: Theory: IARE UCMP notes; Theory: P.K. Mishra

question: Ultrasonic machining (USM) and abrasive-jet machining (AJM) are classed as…
explanation: USM, AJM and water-jet machining are mechanical processes.

question: How is material removed in thermal processes like EDM and LBM?
options: By shearing with a sharp edge
explanation: Thermal energy is applied to a small zone, which melts and vaporises.

question: Electrochemical machining (ECM) is described as the reverse of…
explanation: ECM removes metal by anodic dissolution, the reverse of plating.

question: In most unconventional processes, the tool…
options: Need not be harder than the workpiece
Must be twice as hard as the work
explanation: For example, a soft brass wire cuts hardened steel in wire EDM.

question: In wire EDM, material is removed by…
options: Repeated electric sparks that melt and vaporise metal
Chemicals in the water dissolving it
A rotating abrasive wheel grinding it
A wire sawing through it by friction
explanation: Pulsed sparks between the wire and the work cause thermal erosion.

question: During cutting in wire EDM, the wire electrode and the workpiece…
explanation: There is no mechanical contact and practically no cutting force.

question: What happens if the wire touches the workpiece in wire EDM?
options: The cutting rate doubles at once
A short circuit occurs and no spark forms
explanation: Contact short-circuits the gap, so a small spark gap must be maintained.

question: In wire EDM, the spark gap is kept constant by…
explanation: A servo maintains a gap of roughly 0.025–0.075 mm.

question: If the spark gap in EDM is too large…
options: The wire shorts with the work
explanation: Too large: no spark. Too small: short circuit.

question: In wire EDM, material is removed during…
explanation: The log sheet: during Ton discharge occurs and material is removed.

question: What is the purpose of the pulse-off time (Toff) in EDM?
options: Increases the energy of each following spark
Moves the wire spool faster between sparks
Heats the workpiece so it softens for cutting
Lets the dielectric de-ionise and flushes debris away
explanation: During Toff the gap recovers its insulation and debris is flushed; too short a Toff causes arcing.

question: Which condition must a workpiece satisfy to be cut by wire EDM?
options: It must be soft and ductile
explanation: EDM needs a conductive workpiece; hardness does not matter.

question: Which material CANNOT be cut by wire EDM?
explanation: Non-conductors like glass, plastics and most ceramics cannot be EDMed; hard conductive metals can.

question: In wire EDM, the wire follows the required profile under…
explanation: The log sheet step: enter the required profile through part programming.

question: To cut an internal profile (closed cavity) by wire EDM, you must first…
options: Drill a start hole to thread the wire through
Heat the job until it is red hot
Plate the job with a thin copper layer
Grind the profile roughly to shape
explanation: The wire must pass through the job, so a start hole is needed for internal shapes.

question: Wire EDM can cut tapered sides by…
options: Rotating the table at high speed
Tilting the upper and lower wire guides
Bending the wire into a curve
explanation: WEDM cuts 2-D through-profiles; offsetting the guides gives a taper.

question: The dielectric commonly used in wire EDM is…
explanation: Wire EDM uses deionised water; die-sinking EDM usually uses a hydrocarbon oil such as kerosene.
ref: Theory: Makino EDM wire tutorial; Theory: P.K. Mishra

question: Die-sinking EDM usually uses which dielectric?
options: A hydrocarbon oil such as kerosene
explanation: Die-sinking EDM: oil (kerosene); wire EDM: deionised water.

question: Which of these is NOT a function of the dielectric in EDM?
options: Supplying metal ions to plate the work
explanation: The dielectric insulates, concentrates the spark, cools and flushes. Supplying metal ions is what a plating bath does.

question: Why is the water in wire EDM continuously deionised?
options: To colour the water for easy viewing
To make it heavier so it flushes better
To add metal ions that help the spark
Tap water is too conductive for proper sparking
explanation: Ions make water conductive; the dielectric must insulate until breakdown, so it is filtered and deionised.

question: The wire electrode in wire EDM is usually made of…
explanation: Brass (often zinc-coated) is common; copper, molybdenum or tungsten are also used.

question: Typical wire diameter in wire EDM is about…
explanation: Very thin wires, about 0.05–0.3 mm (commonly 0.25 mm), are used.

question: In wire EDM, the wire is…
options: Fed continuously and used only once
explanation: The wire erodes, so fresh wire is fed from a spool to a take-up and not reused.

question: The wire in wire EDM is held accurately above and below the job by…
explanation: Upper and lower guides position the wire; they can be offset for taper cuts.

question: The kerf width in wire EDM equals…
explanation: The wire erodes a slot as wide as itself plus a spark gap on each side.

question: A 0.25 mm brass wire cuts with a spark gap of 0.03 mm. What is the kerf width?
explanation: Kerf = d + 2g = 0.25 + 2(0.03) = 0.31 mm. Forgetting the factor 2 gives 0.28 mm.

question: A wire EDM cut produces a kerf of 0.36 mm with a 0.30 mm wire. What is the spark gap?
In wire EDM programming, the wire path is offset from the drawn profile by…
explanation: The wire centre must stay (radius + gap) away from the finished edge.

question: For a 0.25 mm wire and a 0.025 mm spark gap, what wire offset is programmed?
Which of these is NOT a wire EDM machining parameter?
explanation: WEDM parameters: Ton, Toff, peak current, voltage, wire tension, wire feed and flushing. There is no rotating spindle.

question: In EDM, increasing the peak current and pulse-on time generally…
options: Decreases cutting rate and improves finish
Has no effect on the cut
Increases cutting rate but roughens the surface
explanation: Higher spark energy removes more metal per spark, giving bigger craters and a rougher surface.

question: If wire tension in wire EDM is too LOW…
options: The wire vibrates and accuracy suffers
The wire always breaks at once
explanation: Low tension causes vibration and inaccuracy; too high causes breakage.

question: A main cause of wire breakage and poor finish in wire EDM is…
explanation: Poor flushing leaves debris, causing arcing and wire breakage.

question: In EDM, the thin re-solidified layer left on the machined surface is called the…
explanation: Each spark leaves a crater; melted metal re-solidifies as a recast layer over a heat-affected zone.

question: Which is an advantage of wire EDM?
options: It is the fastest metal-removal process
No cutting force, so thin delicate parts can be cut
It needs no dielectric fluid at all
It cuts any material, including glass
explanation: Advantages: complex 2-D profiles, high accuracy and finish, no burrs, no cutting force, hard materials.

question: Which is a limitation of wire EDM?
options: It cannot cut hardened tool steel
It leaves heavy burrs on every edge
Only electrically conductive materials can be cut
It needs a tool harder than the job
explanation: Limitations: conductive materials only, slow removal, recast layer/HAZ, wire cost.

question: Wire EDM is widely used for making…
options: Press-tool dies, punches and extrusion dies
explanation: Tool and die making is the main application; also gears and aerospace/medical parts.

question: How does die-sinking EDM differ from wire EDM?
options: A shaped electrode sinks a 3-D cavity instead of a wire cutting a profile
It uses a laser beam instead of electric sparks
It works without any dielectric in the gap
It needs no electric power supply at all
explanation: Die-sinking: shaped copper/graphite electrode, usually in oil. Wire EDM: moving wire, 2-D through-profiles, deionised water.

question: In laser cutting, material is removed by…
options: A spinning cutter shearing the metal
A focused beam melting or vaporising the metal
Sparks between a wire and the metal
explanation: The beam melts/vaporises a narrow zone; a coaxial assist-gas jet blows the melt out of the kerf.

question: LASER stands for…
options: Low-Angle Surface Erosion by Reflected Radiation
Light And Sound Energy Release by Stimulation
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Linear Amplification by Spark Emission of Radiation
explanation: LASER = Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.

question: The gain medium of a fiber laser is…
options: A sealed tube of CO₂ gas
An optical fiber doped with ytterbium
explanation: Fiber lasers are solid-state lasers with a Yb-doped fiber.

question: The wavelength of a fiber laser is about…
explanation: Fiber ≈ 1.06 µm; CO₂ ≈ 10.6 µm.

question: Why are fiber lasers preferred over CO₂ lasers for cutting metal sheet?
options: Metals absorb the shorter 1.06 µm wavelength much better
Fiber lasers have the longer wavelength of the two
Fiber lasers need no assist gas for cutting
CO₂ laser beams cannot be focused at all
explanation: Metals absorb ~1 µm light far better than 10.6 µm light.

question: CO₂ lasers are widely used for cutting…
options: Non-metals such as wood, acrylic and plastics
explanation: CO₂ lasers (10.6 µm) suit non-metals.

question: In a fiber laser cutting machine, the beam reaches the cutting head through…
options: A rigid steel pipe of mirrors only
explanation: The beam is delivered by fiber; the path is CNC-programmed.

question: Since laser cutting is non-contact, it has…
options: No tool wear and no cutting force
A need for a sharp cutter
A large clamping force on the job
explanation: Non-contact processing: no tool wear, no mechanical force.

question: Which assist gas is normally used for laser cutting mild steel?
explanation: O₂ reacts exothermically with iron, adding heat for faster/thicker cuts (with an oxide layer on the edge).

question: Which assist gas is used for clean, oxide-free cuts in stainless steel and aluminium?
explanation: N₂ is inert; the laser supplies all the energy and the edges stay bright.

question: Why does oxygen assist gas allow faster cutting of mild steel?
options: Its exothermic reaction with iron adds extra heat
It cools the kerf faster than nitrogen
It is heavier than nitrogen, so it pushes
It increases the wavelength of the laser
explanation: The iron–oxygen reaction releases heat, supplementing the laser energy.

question: What is the drawback of cutting mild steel with oxygen assist gas?
options: The kerf becomes very wide always
The cut cannot go through the sheet
The focusing lens melts at once
An oxide layer forms on the cut edge
explanation: Oxygen leaves an oxidised edge; nitrogen gives oxide-free edges.

question: A cheap assist-gas option for thin sheets is…
explanation: Compressed air is a low-cost option for thin material.

question: Besides removing molten metal, the assist gas also…
options: Supplies the laser light to the head
Protects the lens from spatter and cools the cut
Polishes the sheet surface after cutting
explanation: The coaxial gas jet keeps spatter off the optics and cools the cut zone.

question: Which of these is NOT a laser-cutting parameter?
explanation: Parameters: power, speed, focal position, gas type and pressure, nozzle diameter, stand-off.

question: In the laser cutting head, the beam is focused to a small spot by the…
explanation: The collimator makes the beam parallel; the focusing lens concentrates it to a spot.

question: Stand-off distance in laser cutting is the gap between…
options: The lens and the end of the fiber
Two successive passes of the beam
The nozzle tip and the workpiece surface
The machine table and the floor
explanation: It affects gas flow and focus position.

question: Compared with other thermal cutting, laser cutting gives…
options: A wide kerf and a large HAZ
A narrow kerf and a small heat-affected zone
No kerf at all, only a line mark
A thick recast layer on every cut
explanation: Kerf is a few tenths of a mm and the HAZ is small.

question: In laser cutting, "dross" means…
options: The coating on the optical fiber
Re-solidified metal stuck to the bottom edge
The pressure of the assist gas
explanation: Dross is melt that did not get blown away; striations are lines on the cut face.

question: If the laser cutting speed is too HIGH, the likely result is…
options: Burning and melting of the nozzle
A very wide kerf and a large HAZ
An incomplete cut and dross on the underside
A perfect cut with no change at all
explanation: Too fast: the beam cannot cut through, leaving dross. Too slow: wide kerf and big HAZ.

question: Which is an advantage of fiber laser cutting?
options: High speed and precision with intricate shapes
It cuts any thickness of plate easily
Its equipment is very cheap to buy
It needs no electricity to operate
explanation: Advantages: speed, precision, narrow kerf, small HAZ, no tool wear, intricate shapes.

question: Which is a limitation of fiber laser cutting?
options: It always needs a sharp cutting tool
It cannot cut mild steel at all
It works only on wood and paper
High equipment cost and a thickness limit
explanation: Limitations: high cost, thickness limits, reflective metals can be difficult, fumes.

question: Which metals are often difficult to laser cut because they reflect the beam?
explanation: Highly reflective metals like copper and brass reflect much of the beam.

question: Which eye protection is required near a fiber laser cutter?
options: Laser safety goggles rated for its wavelength
No protection is needed with the door open
explanation: Wear laser goggles of the correct wavelength rating and never look into the beam.

question: Which is a laser-cutting safety rule?
options: Keep the enclosure closed and use fume extraction
Switch off the extraction to save power
Put hands on the bed to steady the sheet
Look into the beam to check focus
explanation: Keep the enclosure closed, extract fumes, keep hands off the bed, and watch for fire.

question: What are the objectives of the ME-106 unconventional machining practice?
options: To study ECM and ultrasonic machining (USM)
To study plasma cutting and water-jet cutting
To study CNC milling and 3D printing machines
To study wire EDM and the fiber laser cutting machine
explanation: Objectives: 1 study wire electrical discharge machining; 2 study the fiber laser cutting machine.

question: What job is cut on the wire EDM in the ME-106 lab?
options: A ring cut from metal sheet
A square 10 mm × 10 mm, 5 mm thick
explanation: The log sheet drawing: EDM square 10 × 10 mm with 5 mm thickness.

question: What job is cut on the fiber laser in the ME-106 lab?
explanation: The log sheet drawing shows a laser-cut ring.

question: What is the volume of the 10 × 10 × 5 mm wire-EDM square?
The 10 × 10 mm EDM square is cut out of a plate along its full perimeter. What length of cut does the wire travel?
explanation: Perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40 mm.

question: Which of these is listed in the ME-106 wire EDM tool list?
explanation: Tools: wire-cut EDM machine, clamping tool, clamping wire, power supply, dielectric fluid supply, part programming, wire electrode.

question: Which item is NOT in the ME-106 wire EDM tool list?
explanation: Assist gas belongs to laser cutting.

question: What is the FIRST step of the ME-106 wire EDM procedure?
options: Remove and inspect the machined job
Enter the profile in the part program
Clamp the workpiece properly on the machine
Apply pulsed voltage to the wire
explanation: Step 1: clamp the workpiece properly on the EDM machine.

question: Which step comes immediately after clamping the job in the ME-106 wire EDM procedure?
options: Fix and tension the wire electrode
explanation: Step 2: fix and tension the wire electrode.

question: In the ME-106 wire EDM procedure, which step comes before entering the profile through part programming?
options: The wire completing the programmed cut
Supplying the dielectric fluid to the machining zone
Removing and inspecting the machined job
Applying pulsed voltage to the wire
explanation: Steps 3–5: set parameters → supply dielectric → enter profile by part programming.

question: In the ME-106 wire EDM procedure, the machining parameters are set…
options: After the machined job has been removed
Only after the whole cut is complete
After fixing the wire and before supplying dielectric
Before the workpiece has been clamped
explanation: Step 3: set the required machining parameters.

question: What must be maintained between the wire and workpiece during the cut (step 6)?
explanation: Step 6: maintain a small spark gap between wire and workpiece.

question: In step 7 of the ME-106 wire EDM procedure, what is applied between the wire and the job?
explanation: Step 7: apply pulsed electrical voltage between the wire and workpiece.

question: According to the ME-106 log sheet, how is material removed in wire EDM (step 8)?
options: By the wire rubbing the job
By the heat generated by the sparks
By chemical attack of the water
explanation: Step 8: material is removed due to the heat generated by the sparks.

question: What is the LAST step of the ME-106 wire EDM procedure?
options: Clamp the workpiece on the machine
Fix and tension the wire electrode
Remove and inspect the machined job
explanation: Step 11 (the last): remove and inspect the machined job.

question: In the ME-106 wire EDM procedure, how is the profile completed (step 10)?
options: The wire moves along the programmed profile
The job is turned on a centre lathe
The operator saws it out by hand
The table rotates the job like a lathe
explanation: Step 10: the wire moves according to the programmed profile and completes the cut.

question: What is the correct order of the ME-106 wire EDM procedure?
options: Fix & tension wire → clamp job → apply pulses → set parameters → enter profile → supply dielectric → keep spark gap → cut → remove & inspect
Clamp job → fix & tension wire → set parameters → supply dielectric → enter profile → keep spark gap → apply pulses → cut → remove & inspect
Supply dielectric → set parameters → clamp job → cut → fix & tension wire → enter profile → keep spark gap → apply pulses → remove & inspect
Enter profile → apply pulses → clamp job → supply dielectric → fix & tension wire → set parameters → keep spark gap → cut → remove & inspect
explanation: From the Unconventional log sheet.

question: What is the FIRST step of the ME-106 fiber laser procedure?
options: Start the laser beam and cut the path
Inspect the profile of the cut piece
Clamp the metal sheet properly on the bed
Do a dry run to check the position
explanation: Step 1: clamp the metal sheet properly on the machine bed.

question: Where is the cutting profile set for the fiber laser?
explanation: Step 2: set the required cutting profile in the CNC controller.

question: Which settings are made in step 3 of the ME-106 fiber laser procedure?
options: Ton, Toff and tension of the wire
Laser power, cutting speed and assist gas
Grit, grade and bond of the wheel
Index plate, crank and sector arms
explanation: Step 3: set laser power, cutting speed and assist gas.

question: In the ME-106 fiber laser procedure, how is the beam focused on the job?
options: By moving the sheet by hand
explanation: Step 4: focus the laser beam on the workpiece through the remote.

question: Why is a dry run done before laser cutting?
options: To clean the lens with the assist gas
To heat the sheet so it cuts more easily
To cool the nozzle before the cut starts
To check the laser will cut at the correct place
explanation: Step 5 and precaution 6: check by dry cutting (dry run) whether the laser will cut in the correct place.

question: Which step comes immediately AFTER the dry run in the fiber laser procedure?
options: Clamp the metal sheet on the bed
Set the laser power and cutting speed
Start the beam and cut along the programmed path
Focus the beam using the remote
explanation: Step 6: start the laser beam and cut along the programmed path.

question: What is the LAST step of the ME-106 fiber laser procedure?
options: Remove the cut piece and inspect the profile
Set the type and pressure of assist gas
Clamp the metal sheet on the machine bed
Do a dry run along the programmed path
explanation: Step 7: remove the cut piece and inspect the profile.

question: What is the correct order of the ME-106 fiber laser procedure?
options: Focus beam → cut → clamp sheet → dry run → set profile in CNC → set power, speed & gas → remove & inspect
Clamp sheet → set profile in CNC → set power, speed & gas → focus beam → dry run → cut → remove & inspect
Set power, speed & gas → clamp sheet → cut → focus beam → dry run → set profile in CNC → remove & inspect
Dry run → clamp sheet → set profile in CNC → cut → focus beam → set power, speed & gas → remove & inspect
explanation: From the Unconventional log sheet p.2.

question: Which precaution applies to both wire EDM and laser cutting in the ME-106 log sheet?
options: Do not rotate the crank backwards
explanation: Precaution 1: clamp the workpiece properly.

question: Which wire EDM precaution is listed on the ME-106 log sheet?
options: Maintain correct wire tension and spark gap
Keep the wire touching the job
explanation: Precaution 2: maintain correct wire tension and spark gap.

question: What must be ensured about the dielectric during wire EDM?
options: A continuous supply of dielectric fluid
It is switched off during the cut
explanation: Precaution 3: ensure continuous supply of dielectric fluid.

question: Which electrical settings must be set correctly in wire EDM (log sheet)?
explanation: Precaution 4: set Ton, Toff and peak current correctly.

question: Which laser precaution is listed on the ME-106 log sheet?
options: Use oil as the dielectric fluid
Set correct laser power and cutting speed
Keep the wire slack during cutting
Look into the beam to focus it
explanation: Precaution 5: set the correct laser power and cutting speed.

question:
Assertion (A): Wire EDM can cut hardened tool steel easily.
Reason (R): In EDM the hardness of the workpiece does not affect material removal.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: Both true, and R explains A: removal is by sparks, so only conductivity matters, not hardness.

question:
Assertion (A): Fiber lasers are preferred for cutting metal sheet.
Reason (R): The fiber-laser wavelength (10.6 µm) is longer than that of CO₂ lasers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: A is true but R is false: fiber ≈ 1.06 µm (shorter); CO₂ ≈ 10.6 µm. Metals absorb the shorter wavelength better.
ref: Theory: industry sources (GWK, Xometry); Theory: industry sources

question:
Assertion (A): Nitrogen is used as assist gas for stainless steel.
Reason (R): Nitrogen gives clean, oxide-free cut edges.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: Both true and R explains A.

question: In wire EDM, the wire must touch the workpiece to cut it.
explanation: False. A spark gap is kept; contact would short-circuit.
ref: Theory: Kalpakjian; Unconventional log sheet p.1

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled B?
explanation: B = Upper wire guide. Guides the wire accurately above the job (can tilt for taper cuts).

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled C?
explanation: C = Lower wire guide. Guides the wire accurately below the job.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled D?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled E?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled F?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled G?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled H?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled I?

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled J?
explanation: J = Used-wire take-up. Collects the eroded wire, which is not reused.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled K?
explanation: K = Kerf (cut slot). Width = wire diameter + 2 × spark gap.

question: In the figure, which label shows the upper wire guide?
explanation: B = Upper wire guide. Guides the wire accurately above the job (can tilt for taper cuts).

question: In the figure, which label shows the dielectric nozzle?
explanation: F = Dielectric nozzle. Flushes deionised water through the gap to cool and remove debris.

explanation: I = CNC / servo control. Follows the part program and keeps the spark gap constant.

question: In the figure, which label shows the kerf (cut slot)?

options: Guides the wire accurately above the job (can tilt for taper cuts)
Flushes deionised water through the gap to cool and remove debris
Moves the job along the programmed profile under CNC control
Thin brass wire (≈0.05–0.3 mm) that sparks against the job without touching it
explanation: F = Dielectric nozzle. Flushes deionised water through the gap to cool and remove debris.

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled I?

Collects the eroded wire, which is not reused
Follows the part program and keeps the spark gap constant

label: I

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled J?
options: Collects the eroded wire, which is not reused
Moves the job along the programmed profile under CNC control
Flushes deionised water through the gap to cool and remove debris
Follows the part program and keeps the spark gap constant
explanation: J = Used-wire take-up. Collects the eroded wire, which is not reused.
label: J

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled H?
options: Follows the part program and keeps the spark gap constant
Applies pulsed DC voltage between wire and work (Ton / Toff)
Feeds fresh wire continuously; the wire is used only once
explanation: H = Pulse power supply. Applies pulsed DC voltage between wire and work (Ton / Toff).
label: H

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled A?
explanation: A = Wire electrode. Moving brass wire; never touches the job.
label: A

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled B?
explanation: B = Spark gap (g). Small gap kept constant by the servo; sparks jump across it.
label: B

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled C?
explanation: C = Spark (discharge). Pulse of energy that melts and vaporises a tiny bit of metal.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled D?
explanation: D = Crater. Small pit left by each spark on the cut surface.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled E?
explanation: E = Debris. Eroded particles flushed away by the dielectric.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled F?
explanation: F = Wire diameter (d). Size of the wire electrode.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled G?
explanation: G = Kerf width. Kerf = d + 2g.

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled H?
explanation: H = Dielectric (deionised water). Insulates until breakdown, cools and flushes the gap.
label: H

question: In the spark-gap figure, the wire diameter F is 0.20 mm and gap B is 0.04 mm. What is kerf width G?
In the spark-gap figure, what fills the gap between the wire and the work?

ref: Theory: Makino EDM wire tutorial; Theory: P.K. Mishra

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled A?
explanation: A = Optical fiber input. Delivers the 1.06 µm beam from the fiber laser source.
label: A

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled B?
explanation: B = Collimating lens. Makes the diverging beam from the fiber parallel.
label: B

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled C?
explanation: C = Focusing lens. Focuses the beam to a tiny, intense spot.
label: C

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled D?
explanation: D = Assist-gas inlet. Supplies O₂, N₂ or air to blow molten metal out of the kerf.
label: D

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled E?
explanation: E = Nozzle. Directs the assist gas coaxially with the beam.
label: E

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled F?
explanation: F = Focal point. Smallest, most intense spot, set on or just in the sheet.
label: F

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled G?
explanation: G = Stand-off distance. Gap between the nozzle tip and the sheet surface.
label: G

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled H?
explanation: H = Kerf. Narrow slot (a few tenths of a mm) cut through the sheet.
label: H

question: In the figure, what is the part labelled I?
explanation: I = Molten metal ejected. Blown out by the assist-gas jet.
label: I

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled B?
options: Delivers the 1.06 µm beam from the fiber laser source
Gap between the nozzle tip and the sheet surface
Supplies O₂, N₂ or air to blow molten metal out of the kerf
Makes the diverging beam from the fiber parallel
explanation: B = Collimating lens. Makes the diverging beam from the fiber parallel.
label: B

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled C?
options: Smallest, most intense spot, set on or just in the sheet
Gap between the nozzle tip and the sheet surface
Delivers the 1.06 µm beam from the fiber laser source
Focuses the beam to a tiny, intense spot
explanation: C = Focusing lens. Focuses the beam to a tiny, intense spot.
label: C

question: In the figure, what is the function of the part labelled D?
options: Makes the diverging beam from the fiber parallel
Focuses the beam to a tiny, intense spot
Supplies O₂, N₂ or air to blow molten metal out of the kerf
Blown out by the assist-gas jet
explanation: D = Assist-gas inlet. Supplies O₂, N₂ or air to blow molten metal out of the kerf.
label: D

question: Which machine was used for the job in panel A?
explanation: A = Wire-cut EDM. Square 10 mm × 10 mm, 5 mm thick.
label: A

question: Which machine was used for the job in panel B?
explanation: B = Fiber laser cutting machine. Ring (annulus) cut from metal sheet.
label: B

question: In the figure, what are the dimensions of the job in panel A?
explanation: Panel A is the wire-EDM square: 10 × 10 mm, 5 mm thick.

question: Which process is shown in panel A?
explanation: A = Die-sinking EDM. Shaped (copper/graphite) electrode sinks a 3-D cavity, usually in oil.
label: A

question: Which process is shown in panel B?
explanation: B = Wire EDM. Moving thin wire cuts a 2-D through-profile, usually in deionised water.
label: B

question: In the EDM comparison figure, which panel normally uses deionised water as the dielectric?
explanation: Panel B (wire EDM) uses deionised water; panel A (die-sinking) usually uses kerosene/oil.
ref: Theory: Makino EDM wire tutorial; Theory: P.K. Mishra
